Theme

School & learning

sum noun

a calculation in arithmetic

also sums, do sums, do a sum, calculation, calculate, work out, compute, computation

classical

Hor. Ars 325: longīs ratiōnibus
Cic. Att. 5.21.11: subdūcāmus summam

ratiō, ratiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a reckoning, a calculation

The reckoning of an account, then any calculation: Horace’s schoolboys learn their fractions longīs ratiōnibus, by long sums. To do a sum is ratiōnem subdūcere or inīre (Lewis & Short); what it comes to is the summa (see amount).

Other words

  • ratiuncula, ratiunculae f. — a little sum, a small reckoning

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 371; Ter. Ph. 36

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    In Cicero a petty reason or a quibble (Lewis & Short).

  • calculus, calculī m. — a reckoning (with counters)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.60: calculīs subductīs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Lael. 58: ad calculōs vocāre (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. calculation

    The pebble moved on the counting board, and so the reckoning itself: calculōs subdūcere, to work out a sum. See also counter.

  • computō, computāre, computāvī, computātum — reckon up, calculate

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 204: dextera digitīs ratiōnem computat; Quint. 1.10.43 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: mostly post-Augustan. A reckoning is computātiō (Quint. 1.10.35).

Examples

  • Beātus videor: subdūxī ratiunculam, quantum aeris mihi sit quantumque aliēnī siet

    I feel a happy man: I’ve done a little sum of how much money I have and how much I owePlaut. Curc. 371–372

  • dextera digitīs ratiōnem computat

    he is doing a sum on the fingers of his right handPlaut. Mil. 204

See also arithmetic, amount, count, problem, subtract, multiply, divide, calculator, counter.
